If sentiment is positive and forecast is trending up, reduce late-period forecast by 1.5–2.0% to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is trending down, increase early-period forecast by 1.0–1.5% to counteract pessimism.  
When sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% for the next 3–5 days.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast shows strong upward momentum, cap late-period peaks at 1.5% below historical max.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is flat or slightly down, add 0.5–1.0% upward bias in mid-period to capture momentum.  
When sentiment is negative and forecast is flat, reduce early-period values by 0.5–1.0% to avoid false confidence.
